summary:
Solar Terminator: Autonomous Solar-Powered Optical Tracking & Redirection System

Solar Terminator is an autonomous robotic prototype that harnesses and redirects concentrated solar energy for deep-space power transmission and planetary defense. Using a precision parabolic solar reflector mounted on a 4-DOF MeArm robotic manipulator, the system tracks targets and projects focused light beams to power rovers in the permanently shadowed craters of the lunar South Pole and propel solar sails. Additionally, high-intensity redirected thermal energy can de-orbit hazardous space debris, deflect incoming meteors, and mitigate agricultural locust swarms from orbit.

Built on an STM32 microcontroller and PCA9685 PWM driver, the hardware is integrated with a ROS 2 and RViz2 simulation and control pipeline. A USB camera paired with C++ and Python computer vision nodes (OpenCV and ONNX Runtime) executes real-time visual servoing to lock onto moving targets. To protect mechanical gears and ensure pinpoint optical alignment over long distances, an S-curve motion trajectory profile eliminates jerky movements, delivering smooth, continuous servo actuation. Simulated with an LED light source, Solar Terminator demonstrates a scalable, fuel-free optical infrastructure for sustainable lunar exploration and orbital safety.

Had also use Chatgpt, Gemini, Drift and Cline to prepare this project.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Solar Terminator is an autonomous, dual-purpose robotic optical tracking and energy redirection prototype. Instead of relying on onboard lasers, chemical propellants or bulky nuclear power systems, it captures ambient sunlight using a lightweight parabolic solar reflector mounted on a 4-DOF MeArm robotic manipulator and redirects a focused beam of light energy onto distant targets.

To simulate and validate orbital operations on Earth, the prototype uses an LED light source to represent the Sun and a USB camera for target acquisition:

  1. Target Detection & Inference: Live video frames are captured via USB camera and processed through an OpenCV and ONNX Runtime computer vision pipeline to detect and classify targets in real time.
  2. Closed-Loop Visual Servoing: Once a target is locked, a visual servoing control loop calculates the angular error between the optical axis and the target's coordinates.
  3. Smooth Trajectory Generation: Rather than sending abrupt step commands that cause mechanical jitter, the controller applies an S-curve velocity profile to generate smooth, continuous acceleration and deceleration curves.
  4. Actuation & Digital Twin: Kinematic commands are transmitted to an STM32 microcontroller driving a PCA9685 PWM controller to actuate the robotic arm, while ROS 2 and RViz2 provide real-time telemetry, visualization, and digital twin synchronization.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Solar Terminator addresses both deep-space exploration bottlenecks and orbital/terrestrial hazards using a single, fuel-free optical architecture:

  • Lunar South Pole Power Beaming: Permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) on the Moon contain vital water ice but receive zero direct sunlight. Orbiting reflector satellites can beam continuous solar energy directly onto lunar rovers and habitats, eliminating the need for heavy batteries or radioisotope heaters.
  • Propellantless Solar Sail Propulsion: Concentrated light beams provide sustained photon pressure to accelerate solar sails beyond what ambient sunlight alone can achieve.
  • Active Space Debris & Meteor Mitigation: Focusing thermal energy onto orbital debris induces surface ablation, creating slight thrust that lowers the object's perigee so it burns up harmlessly in Earth's atmosphere—and offers a non-kinetic deflection method for incoming meteors.
  • Terrestrial Agricultural Protection: Scaled orbital constellations could redirect targeted thermal pulses to disrupt destructive locust swarms before they devastate crops.

Hardware, Software & Tools Used

  • Hardware & Actuation: STM32 microcontroller, PCA9685 16-channel PWM servo driver, 4-DOF MeArm robotic manipulator, lightweight aluminum parabolic solar reflector, USB camera, and high-output LED solar simulator.
  • Languages & Frameworks: C++ (for low-latency inference and control loops), Python (for data preprocessing and node orchestration), and ROS 2.
  • AI, Vision & Simulation: OpenCV, ONNX Runtime, custom-trained object classification models, visual servoing algorithms, S-curve motion profiling, and RViz2 for 3D kinematic visualization.

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Mechanical Preservation via S-Curve Kinematics: Micro-servos with lightweight nylon gears are vulnerable to stripping under sudden torque spikes, and high-frequency vibration ruins long-range optical aim. Implementing S-curve motion profiling solved both problems simultaneously—protecting the hardware while keeping the reflected beam steady on target.
  • Low-Latency Edge Execution: By combining C++ with ONNX Runtime and OpenCV, the vision pipeline avoids heavy interpreter overhead, ensuring deterministic tracking performance suitable for resource-constrained spacecraft avionics.
  • Multi-Mission Versatility: Rather than building a single-purpose satellite, the design proves that one precision-pointed optical reflector platform can serve as modular infrastructure for lunar power, deep-space propulsion, planetary defense, and Earth observation/intervention.

Had also use Chatgpt, Gemini, Drift and Cline to prepare this project.
